page.layout: One block of verse in roman type, full width, with a running head at the top; below the text a gathering mark at the foot left. No marginal notes.

p.i: Quam tua non auxit, tua non industria seuit, Sed natam altera nox, denatámque altera vidit, Hanc perisse doles, hanc plurimus expetis herbã. Mene igitur, mene Assyrij qui maximus author Sanguinis, immensa qui fundamenta locauit Niniues, cœlóque arces & mœnia vexi, Sauire, & tantam subito refcindere gentem? Et quota pars laua quid distet dextera nouit? Si tibi non herba facilis iactura, neque vmbra, Qua tandem Assyrios seniam seruare petentes Inuidia est? potiorne meis tua plantula regnis? En qui vmbra gemit amissa, foliisque caducis, Is ruere imperia, & magnas desiderat vrbes. Ipsa adeo & culpa vacua, & rationis egena, O demens, mihi si nescis, animalia cura.
Dixerat: his tandem monitis edoctus Ionas Conticuit, certóque Deum veneratus honore est: Infignem bonitate Deum, qui parcere nautis, Parcere & Assyriis, & parcere pronus Iona.

Excrere, ô, duris aliquis mortalibus heros, Aut nostram tu Bezza decus pete sydera ferò, Vtilibus qui vera minis promissa remiscens Ad meliora voces, & numine plenus eodem Impia vicina subducas secula flamma.

page.notes: Printed verse with long s rendered as s; "Bezza" and "herba" as printed; "Cc 2" is the signature at the foot. Some words in the stanza beginning "Quam" are uncertain, notably "Ponno" ... none marked. Greek-style ampersand-like signs (& for et) rendered as &.
